title: Best Practices for Testing and Rolling Out SSL/TLS Inspection

blocks.text: As a best practice, Zscaler recommends that you enable SSL/TLS Inspection in a small location or test lab before enabling it on all locations in your organization. This allows you to test your deployment of SSL/TLS Inspection with a select number of users.
To enable SSL/TLS Inspection, first deploy the Zscaler or custom intermediate root certificate. Then, enable SSL/TLS Inspection for the location or sublocation you are using for testing.

Before testing SSL/TLS Inspection, define the set of users you want to use for testing. For example, you can choose users from the IT department, such as application authors and owners, support staff members, proxy team members, or security team members. You can also choose managers and end users from non-IT departments.

blocks.item: Compile a list of the websites and applications that your organization uses for everyday operations. Remember to include vendor sites and applications.
Enable SSL/TLS Inspection for the websites and applications from the list by configuring the SSL/TLS Inspection policy, and then have the users test them.

blocks.text: When you are configuring the SSL/TLS Inspection policy, you are specifying the URL categories or applications that you do not want the service to inspect. For example, if you want to enable SSL/TLS Inspection for the Legal Liability categories only, then select the Do Not Inspect action for all the URL categories except the Legal Liability categories in your SSL/TLS Inspection rule. The Zscaler service does not perform SSL/TLS Inspection on the specified URL categories, but does perform SSL/TLS Inspection on the Legal Liability categories.

blocks.item: You might need to exempt some sites for SSL/TLS Inspection permanently, or you might need to report sites to Zscaler Support to identify the cause of failure.

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends not to exempt the Miscellaneous or Unknown category for SSL/TLS Inspection if the traffic forwarded to Zscaler uses transparent proxy mode. In transparent mode, policies on both SNI and IP addresses are evaluated for exemption from SSL/TLS Inspection. Exempting SSL/TLS Inspection for the Miscellaneous or Unknown category exempts almost all traffic from SSL/TLS Inspection as most IP addresses are categorized as miscellaneous or unknown. However, in the case of explicit traffic forwarding, Zscaler evaluates the policies only based on SNI and does not exempt traffic from SSL/TLS Inspection based on IP address categories. To learn more, see Choosing Traffic Forwarding Methods.

blocks.item: After testing the list of websites and applications, test SSL/TLS Inspection for the URL categories. As a best practice, Zscaler recommends that you enable SSL/TLS Inspection for only certain URL categories at a time, and include the rest of the categories in the list of URL categories for which SSL/TLS transactions are not to be decrypted. Then, when your organization is ready, enable SSL/TLS Inspection for all URL categories.

blocks.text: Some organizations choose to bypass SSL/TLS Inspection for Finance and Health URL categories due to privacy concerns. Zscaler recommends that you enable SSL/TLS Inspection for all URL categories.
Enable and test SSL/TLS Inspection for the URL categories in the following order of phases:
Before testing the URL categories in phase 2, remember to keep SSL/TLS inspection enabled for the URL categories in phase 1.
Before testing the URL categories in phase 3, remember to keep SSL/TLS inspection enabled for the URL categories in phases 1 and 2.
